newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says will delay insurance market change.
newsitem.headline: Japan says will delay insurance market change.

text.p: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) said in a statement early on Tuesday that it would delay the go-ahead until the end of December for newly established subsidiaries of major Japanese insurance firms to issue personal accident policies and other products in the so-called "third-sector" niche insurance market.

Subsidiaries of Japanese life insurers would not be allowed to issue personal accident insurance policies until the end of December, and those of non-life insurers would similarly not be able to sell insurance policies covering only medical treatment or cancer until the year-end, it said.

The Japanese government had given permission to domestic life and non-life insurers to establish and start operations at subsidiaries in each other's sectors on Tuesday, and it was due to set conditions on their operations by then.

The latest conditions unveiled by the ministry early on Tuesday were designed to ease tension with the United States in a long-simmering bilateral dispute over how to open up Tokyo's $382 billion insurance market.

Washington has accused Tokyo of reneging on a 1994 bilateral pact by moving to deregulate Japan's "third sector" market, in which foreign firms have a strong foothold, before opening its primary life and casualty markets.
